name: Subclavian artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Vertebral artery
notes: First and most posterior branch of the subclavian artery; ascends through the transverse foramina of the cervical vertebrae (a documented data/skeleton/bones.json landmark) from C6 upward, alongside the muscles it supplies segmentally along the way. Modeled as a leaf here since its intracranial continuation (joining the contralateral vertebral a. to form the basilar artery, supplying the brain) is out of scope for this musculoskeletal-focused atlas, consistent with data/vascular/head_neck_arterial.json's internal carotid artery leaf for the same reason.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.8; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Axillary artery
notes: Continuation of subclavian a. distal to the 1st rib; divided into 3 parts by pectoralis minor.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Superior thoracic artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Thoracoacromial artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Lateral thoracic artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Subscapular artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Circumflex scapular artery
notes: Major contributor to the scapular anastomosis (collateral pathway around the shoulder).
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Anterior circumflex humeral artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Posterior circumflex humeral artery
notes: Accompanies axillary nerve through the quadrangular space.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Suprascapular artery
notes: Branch of the thyrocervical trunk of the subclavian a., not the axillary a.; crosses over the superior transverse scapular ligament (nerve passes under it -- classic mnemonic 'artery over, nerve under').
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Brachial artery
notes: Continuation of axillary a. distal to teres major; runs in the medial bicipital groove with the median nerve.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Profunda brachii (deep brachial) artery
notes: Accompanies the radial nerve in the spiral groove.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Superior ulnar collateral artery
notes: Part of the elbow (cubital) anastomosis; accompanies the ulnar nerve.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Inferior ulnar collateral artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Radial collateral artery
notes: Terminal branch of profunda brachii; part of the elbow anastomosis.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Middle collateral artery
notes: Other terminal branch of profunda brachii; supplies triceps and the elbow anastomosis.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Radial artery
notes: Brachial a. terminal branch (lateral); palpable at the wrist (radial pulse).
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Radial recurrent artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Ulnar artery
notes: Brachial a. terminal branch (medial), larger than the radial a.; gives off the common interosseous a.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Anterior ulnar recurrent artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Posterior ulnar recurrent artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Common interosseous artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Anterior interosseous artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Posterior interosseous artery
supplies_or_drains: extensor carpi ulnaris, other posterior forearm extensors
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Interosseous recurrent artery
notes: Ascends posterior to the elbow to complete the elbow (cubital) anastomosis with the profunda brachii's middle collateral branch.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Superficial palmar arch
notes: Predominantly formed by the ulnar artery, completed (variably) by the superficial palmar branch of the radial artery.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Common palmar digital arteries
notes: Arise from the superficial arch, each dividing into 2 proper palmar digital arteries.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Deep palmar arch
notes: Predominantly formed by the radial artery, completed by the deep branch of the ulnar artery (anastomosis target simplified to the ulnar_a_r trunk node); gives princeps pollicis a. and palmar metacarpal aa.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Princeps pollicis artery
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
